title: India hosts IORA foreign ministers' meeting; Supreme Court orders stronger food warning labels; Rahul Madan named next IBBI chief

morning.line: It's Friday, the last school day of the week! Delhi-NCR wakes up to a misty, chilly morning and 'poor' air, so cover up and limit long outdoor runs.
morning.thought: Small labels can make big differences. When we read before we choose, whether it is a food packet or a news story, we make wiser decisions.

day.name: This day in history: Alfred Nobel signs his will (27 November 1895)
day.about: On 27 November 1895, in Paris, Swedish scientist Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite, signed his will. He left most of his fortune to set up prizes for those who bring the 'greatest benefit to humankind'. The first Nobel Prizes were given in 1901. Rabindranath Tagore became the first Indian (and first Asian) Nobel laureate in 1913.

word.meaning: (noun) avoiding too much of something; keeping things within sensible limits.
word.example: Eating chips in moderation is fine, but a packet with a 'High Salt' label is a reminder not to overdo it.

morning.task: Pick up any packaged snack at home and read its label. Note down how much sugar, fat and salt it has per 100 g, and decide whether it should get a 'High' warning.

headlines.title: India hosts the 25th Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Council of Ministers meeting in New Delhi.
headlines.summary: Foreign ministers from Indian Ocean countries, including Seychelles, Mauritius and Sri Lanka, arrived in New Delhi on 26 November for the IORA Council of Ministers meeting. IORA brings together 23 member countries and 12 dialogue partners. India is the chair of IORA for 2025-2027. The ministers will discuss the group's future direction and new areas of cooperation in the Indian Ocean region.
headlines.gk: IORA was formed in 1997 and its secretariat is in Ebene, Mauritius. The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean in the world.

headlines.title: Supreme Court tells FSSAI to strengthen front-of-pack warning labels on packaged food.
headlines.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to make front-of-package labels on packaged food stronger. The labels must highlight three nutrients of concern: total sugar, saturated fat and salt. Each one should get its own hexagon-shaped symbol with a picture and a warning such as 'High Sugar', 'High Fat' or 'High Salt'. The aim is to help shoppers make healthier choices at a glance.
headlines.gk: FSSAI is a statutory body set up under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It works under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is headquartered in New Delhi.

headlines.title: Zambia's police ban a protest against moves to remove presidential term limits.
headlines.summary: Police in Zambia banned a march planned by civil society groups, saying it could clash with a rival pro-government rally. Groups close to the ruling party have asked parliament to remove the limit on how many terms a president can serve. President Hakainde Hichilema's second and final term ends in 2031. Changing the Constitution needs a two-thirds majority in parliament, which the ruling party does not have.
headlines.gk: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa with Lusaka as its capital. The Victoria Falls lie on its border with Zimbabwe.

headlines.title: El Nino-charged king tides and storms batter the US West Coast with record water levels.
headlines.summary: Very high 'king tides' and storms hit the west coast of the USA this week. NOAA said Charleston in Oregon recorded its highest-ever coastal water level, and San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara saw some of their highest levels on record. A pier at Pacifica near San Francisco collapsed after being hit by a wave. Scientists say a strong El Nino and climate change are making such tides more damaging.
headlines.gk: King tides are the highest tides of the year, when the Sun and Moon line up with the Earth. El Nino is a warming of the eastern Pacific Ocean that often weakens India's monsoon.

headlines.title: Rishabh Pant, Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal climb into the ICC Test batting top 10.
headlines.summary: New ICC Test rankings came out after India's drawn first Test against New Zealand. Rishabh Pant rose to 6th after scoring 128, Shubman Gill moved up three places to 7th and Yashasvi Jaiswal jumped five places to 9th. Fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah rose to joint 2nd among Test bowlers. KL Rahul, who scored 136, moved up to 25th among batters.
headlines.gk: The International Cricket Council (ICC) is the world governing body of cricket and is headquartered in Dubai.

headlines.title: Eight teams reach the quarter-finals of the 43rd Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar.
headlines.summary: The 43rd Surjit Hockey Tournament is being played in Jalandhar, Punjab. In league matches, Rail Coach Factory beat BSF Jalandhar 4-1 and Punjab Police beat Indian Navy 4-1, while Bharat Petroleum and Army drew 0-0. Eight teams, including Indian Oil, Punjab Police, Indian Air Force and Rail Coach Factory, have made it to the quarter-finals.
headlines.gk: India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in men's hockey, the most by any country. Hockey is often called India's national game, though no law officially declares it so.

headlines.title: Rahul Madan named the next Chairperson of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI).
headlines.summary: Rahul Madan, Managing Director of the Indian Institute of Insolvency Professionals of ICAI, has been designated as the next Chairperson of IBBI, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs announced. He succeeds Jayanti Prasad, who has held additional charge since Ravi Mittal retired on 12 September 2026. Madan is a chartered accountant, cost accountant and insolvency professional who has worked at SBI, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank.
headlines.gk: IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. It works under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and is headquartered in New Delhi.
headlines.exam: Remember: IBBI chair-designate = Rahul Madan; IBBI est. 1 Oct 2016 under IBC 2016; ministry = MCA.

headlines.title: RBI allows SBI Mutual Fund to buy up to 9.99% stake in South Indian Bank.
headlines.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has approved SBI Mutual Fund's proposal to acquire up to 9.99% of the paid-up capital or voting rights of South Indian Bank. The approval comes with conditions under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, RBI's 2025 directions on holding shares in banks, FEMA 1999 and SEBI rules. South Indian Bank has no promoters and is fully held by the public; mutual funds together held 15.13% as of September 2026.
headlines.gk: South Indian Bank is a private sector bank founded in 1929 and headquartered in Thrissur, Kerala. Any holding of 5% or more in an Indian bank needs RBI's prior approval.
headlines.exam: Remember: SBI MF can hold up to 9.99% in South Indian Bank (HQ Thrissur, est. 1929); the law behind it is the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

headlines.title: IRDAI forms a six-member expert committee under Dr Indu Bhushan to review insurance distribution reforms.
headlines.summary: The insurance regulator IRDAI has set up a six-member expert committee chaired by Dr Indu Bhushan, a retired IAS officer and founding CEO of Ayushman Bharat, to review proposed reforms in how insurance is sold. Members include NCAER Director General Suresh Goyal and former SBI Life MD Mahesh Kumar Sharma. The committee's final report is due by 31 December 2026. IRDAI has also reconstituted an advisory committee under Sriram Taranikanti to review how Insurance Ombudsmen are performing.
headlines.gk: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) was set up under the IRDA Act, 1999 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.
headlines.exam: Remember: IRDAI insurance-distribution reform panel chaired by Dr Indu Bhushan; report due 31 Dec 2026.

headlines.title: ICMR's SAMPADA survey finds anaemia among children has dropped to 41.8% from 64% in NFHS-5.
headlines.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) released key findings of its SAMPADA 2023-2025 survey, which covered over 2 lakh people in 183 districts of 35 States and UTs. Anaemia among children stood at 41.8%, compared with 64% in NFHS-5. It was 56% among women, 44% among pregnant women and 19% among men, all lower than in NFHS-5. Severe anaemia was under 2% in most age groups.
headlines.gk: ICMR, India's top body for biomedical research, works under the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Anaemia Mukt Bharat is the government's programme to reduce anaemia.
headlines.exam: Remember: SAMPADA 2023-25 (ICMR) anaemia: children 41.8%, women 56%, pregnant women 44%, men 19%.

headlines.title: India-Nepal joint military exercise Surya Kiran XX begins in Nepal.
headlines.summary: The 20th edition of Exercise Surya Kiran, the joint army exercise between India and Nepal, began on 25 November 2026 at the Nepali Army Battle School in Saljhandi, Rupandehi district. It will run until 8 December 2026. Troops of the Indian Army's 12 Kumaon Regiment and the Nepali Army's Jwala Dal Battalion are taking part. The focus is on disaster management, jungle warfare and humanitarian assistance.
headlines.gk: Surya Kiran is held every year, alternately in India and Nepal. Nepal's Gorkha soldiers also serve in the Indian Army's Gorkha regiments.
headlines.exam: Remember: Surya Kiran XX (India-Nepal army exercise), 25 Nov-8 Dec 2026, Saljhandi, Rupandehi (Nepal); Indian unit 12 Kumaon.

headlines.title: Uttarakhand announces the Baini-Bhuli Yojana to give ₹20,000 to 5.23 lakh rural women.
headlines.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced the Baini-Bhuli Yojana at a Matrishakti Conference in Pipalkoti, Chamoli. Women who are members of self-help groups under the rural livelihood mission will get ₹20,000 in two instalments of ₹10,000 each through Direct Benefit Transfer. About 5.23 lakh rural women are expected to benefit, and the first instalment of ₹523 crore is to be paid in December 2026.
headlines.gk: Uttarakhand was formed on 9 November 2000. Its winter capital is Dehradun and its summer capital is Gairsain (Bhararisain).
headlines.exam: Remember: Baini-Bhuli Yojana (Uttarakhand): ₹20,000 in 2 instalments via DBT to SHG women; ~5.23 lakh beneficiaries.

ai.title: IIT Kanpur and space-tech firm Pixxel team up to use AI on hyperspectral satellite images.
ai.summary: Pixxel, an Indian space technology company, signed an agreement (MoU) with IIT Kanpur at the India International Space Conference 2026 in New Delhi. They will build AI-based models to study hyperspectral images taken from space. These images can help track river health, water resources and changes in how land is used. The work will also combine hyperspectral data with other types of satellite images such as radar and thermal.
ai.gk: A hyperspectral camera records light in hundreds of narrow colour bands, far more than the three (red, green, blue) our eyes use. IIT Kanpur was set up in 1959.

quiz.q: What kind of satellite images will IIT Kanpur and Pixxel analyse with AI?
quiz.explain: The MoU focuses on AI models for hyperspectral image analysis.

ai.title: Google to let schools decide whether students get AI features in its classroom software.
ai.summary: Google says students using its software in classrooms will not get its AI-powered search features unless their school chooses to switch them on. Researchers at the University of North Carolina, who studied how generative AI helps and hurts learning with 30 experts, welcomed giving teachers this control. Professor Jeff Greene said AI can help with steps like making practice quizzes, but he is worried about its effect on younger students.
ai.gk: Generative AI is AI that creates new text, images or sound from what it has learnt. 'Opt in' means a feature stays off until someone chooses to turn it on.

quiz.q: Under Google's change, when will students get AI search features in classroom software?
options: Only if their school opts in
quiz.explain: Schools must choose to switch the AI tools on.

ai.title: Teacher use of AI tools plateaus at 62%, says EdWeek Research Center survey.
ai.summary: A nationally representative survey of 590 US teachers by the EdWeek Research Center found 62% use AI tools in their classrooms this school year, only 1 point more than 61% in 2025. Use had nearly doubled from 34% in 2023 to 61% in 2025. By October, 64% of teachers had attended at least one training session on AI. Experts say unclear guidance from school leaders is slowing further growth.
ai.gk: EdWeek (Education Week) is a US news organisation covering school education. India's NEP 2020 calls for teaching coding and computational thinking from the middle stage.
ai.exam: Remember: EdWeek survey 2026: 62% of US teachers use AI (61% in 2025, 34% in 2023).

quiz.q: What share of US teachers use AI tools in class, as per the latest EdWeek survey?

ai.title: Cashfree Payments launches a wallet that lets personal AI agents pay bills for users.
ai.summary: Cashfree Payments has launched Cashfree Wallet, a prepaid digital wallet that lets a user's personal AI agent make payments on their behalf within limits the user sets. More than 100 AI agents and bot builders are connected through its AgentPay MCP server. The invite-only beta supports bill payments such as electricity, broadband, gas, FASTag and postpaid mobile.
ai.gk: Cashfree Payments was founded in 2015 and is based in Bengaluru; it holds an RBI licence for Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs). MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, a standard for connecting AI agents to tools.
ai.exam: Remember: Cashfree Wallet = prepaid wallet for AI-agent payments via AgentPay MCP server; Cashfree is an RBI-licensed PPI issuer (Bengaluru, 2015).

quiz.q: What is special about the new Cashfree Wallet?
options: Personal AI agents can pay bills from it
It is only for foreign tourists
quiz.explain: It lets users' AI agents make payments within set limits.
